newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-EAGLES AIM TO UPSET WALES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-EAGLES AIM TO UPSET WALES.

text.p: The United States hope local knowledge will boost their chances when they face Wales at Cardiff Arms Park on Saturday.
There are seven British-based players in the Eagles line-up, led by captain Dan Lyle who has impressed since joining English champions Bath and is already looking towards the 1999 World Cup.

"Those guys involved over here, me included, are clearly enjoying and learning from the experience," said Lyle. "We hope to realise the long-term benefits in next year's World Cup qualifying campaign."
Flanker Lyle, 26, captains his country for the fourth time and has overseen a steady, if unspectacular, improvement in fortunes.
They crushed Japan 74-5 in San Francisco last year, lost to Argentina by only three points and led Ireland at halftime in Georgia before succumbing to a narrow defeat.

"We are generally pleased with our progress," said coach Jack Clark. "The team has consistently improved in all facets of play, but we've set high standards for ourselves. The next step in our development will not be easy but it will be the step that turns narrow defeats into victories."
With regular captain Jonathan Humphreys suspended, Wales will be led by centre Scott Gibbs in their final warm-up before next weekend's opening Five Nations encounter with Scotland.
